searchText: We found a bug with how we handle the supernode flag yesterday and are working on a fix. When we implemented validator custody it overrode the supernode behavior. He was working on it when I went to sleep, will check on progress when it's morning hours for him. Should have a fix asap we had some backfill issues i can acknowledge that, mostly because i hadn't got enough time to test our column-syncer and there was a known bug where nimbus itself crashed while range downloading columns in case of supernodes, and later did proceed with sync, as in it advanced slots. eventually, it will be fixed but not right away, as the testing is taking time. Did someone get time to do a root cause analysis though? Which block did things start failing? What actually went wrong in that block? What follow up bugs caused us to never re-heal? Clearly there are sync and/or custody bugs. However neither of those are really root causes imo, something must have knocked the network out at a certain height. Who on Prysm should i be tagging? <@363800010518822915> (since manu is ooo right now) minor spec diff i guess, lighthouse responds to `/eth/v1/beacon/blocks/head`. Other clients deprecated `v1`, they only respond to `v2`. However each one throws a different error for `v1`, some respond with 404, some null. Would be good to deprecate together on the spec + to align on the err code post deprecation tbh. Nimbus has usually been using 410 for this root cause peerdas-devnet-6 I'm confused, no call in 30 minutes, right? we get back to utc midday call? Yes that's right: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1491 prysm-nethermind-9 for e.g responds to `localhost:5052/eth/v2/beacon/blocks/head` with: ``` {"message":"could not reconstruct full execution payload to create signed beacon block: received 0 payload bodies from engine_getPayloadBodiesByRangeV1 with count=1 (start=46139): engine api payload body response is invalid","code":400} ``` not sure if this is to spec either Is there any API manner to get all the peerscores a node has for its peers? if so, we could actually add a visual and display when peers get disconnected (Even if we have no reason, we can derive patterns from this). IMO this would be valuable to debug peerDAS issues, even if its in the debug namespace and just we use it. one issue, at least for Nimbus, is that there are at least two "peer scores", one in Nimbus-the-Ethereum-application and one in libp2p (controlled by the responses to the gossip ignore/reject/etc, but not architecturally intentionally visible) the latter are semi-standardized but not architecturally part of the "CLs" as such, and the former aren't really standardized at all also in general regarding > IMO this would be valuable to debug peerDAS issues, even if its in the debug namespace and just we use it the problem with treating the `debug` namespace this way is that https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/#/Debug/getStateV2 landed there for semi-accidental historical reasons, but it can't really be removed/hidden in a lot of cases, because it's used well outside of "debug" purposes, which means `debug` doesn't function well as a namespace one might, say, turn off or have lower compatibility threshold/guidelines on, so practically, `debug` interfaces tend to end up just as permanent and need just as much design as any others, not just slipped in because, whatever, `debug`, it's just for us PeerDAS testers it might be interesting to have a truly-"debug" namespace, but right now it doesn't exist My understanding is that there’s no “known bug” at the moment. The issue arose because some nodes were running outdated commits. Prysm has since upgraded to a more feature-complete commit. Could each client share an update on their status? The main issue appears to be nodes advertising column subnets as available but being unable to serve them, which prevents other nodes from syncing to the head of the chain One good topic for discussion (I won’t make this one since FOCIL is happening at the same time) is whether we plan to recover devnet6 or just start devnet7 at this point **PeerDAS Breakout Room in 15 min:** - Agenda: https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1491 https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1364170931651481670/1364237336790962247 agreed, i can try bumping up the RAM limit and seeing if that helps - but i think we might be looking at a devnet-7 https://ethereumfoundation.zoom.us/j/82343923303?pwd=aGLyX8xtcVeaDni8mhQi7NNIkzwuUT.1 Yes, it’s a good idea. Idk how we skipped it, probably a blobsidecar spec inspiration thing? But in that case we can make this change for blobsidecars as well? If I’m not missing out on anything We could do something similar for the response too. I think it might save a lot of bandwidth too. But not sure if it's worth the complexity. that's a great idea, but I prefer new request content type, so it won't touch other parts of the spec Could you clarify a bit? Instead of changing `DataColumnIdentifier`, make a new `DataColumnsIdentifier`? could we make new request type as ``` class DataColumnsByRootRequest(Container): block_root: Root indices: List[ColumnIndex, NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS] ``` instead of changing the `DataColumnsIdentifier` structure? Ah I see. We don't really have request types though. We do [this](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/1937aff86b41b5171a9bc3972515986f1bbbf303/specs/fulu/p2p-interface.md?plain=1#L315-L319). ``` ( List[DataColumnIdentifier, MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS] ) ``` But yes. I guess it's essentially the same thing. In your example, the request would be: ``` ( List[DataColumnsByRootRequest, MAX_REQUEST_BLOCKS_DENEB] ) ``` > But yes. I guess it's essentially the same thing. In your example, the request would be: > ( > List[DataColumnsByRootRequest, MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS] > ) we save a lot by not repeating the `roots` field what if the request content be like this instead? ``` ( block_root: Root indices: List[ColumnIndex, NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS] ) ``` looks fair to me Well sort of. We want to request several blocks worth of columns at the same time. This would just be one. that is columns by range no? No, it's not by range. yeah i mean for several blocks we have by range it's supposed to be 1 block (1 block root), just that there will be 1 request fired for downloading multiple column sidecars https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Ng2IrCe28kTt1BnIsjtMlKHq2MHgaja24LhFXSvqfJQ/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.h0hcp5xs4ja8 Here are the meeting minutes from the call today. Unfortunately, the Zoom did not record, so we won't have a video to share. For any clients with column backfill still in progress, is anyone interested in disabling updates to metadata/ENR CGC until nodes are able to serve columns for all blocks? I think some clients are optimistically updating metadata/ENR before all columns are fully custodied -- in Lodestar we added a temp `no-validator-custody` flag to disable this. It might help to determine whether the syncing issues are validator custody-related or otherwise in Teku we update even with lag of few epochs after everything is filled. We will improve it in the future probably to decrease the lag, but we don't start advertising before everything is filled (at least we have a code that should do like this 😀 ) An Easter miracle: https://youtu.be/mbbCjiCIXuQ?feature=shared We found the long lost call 26 recording (collectors item). Made a PR for this: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4284 Would appreciate any feedback.

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: one issue, at least for Nimbus, is that there are at least two "peer scores", one in Nimbus-the-Ethereum-application and one in libp2p (controlled by the responses to the gossip ignore/reject/etc, but not architecturally intentionally visible)

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: the latter are semi-standardized but not architecturally part of the "CLs" as such, and the former aren't really standardized at all

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content:
also in general regarding
> IMO this would be valuable to debug peerDAS issues, even if its in the debug namespace and just we use it

the problem with treating the `debug` namespace this way is that https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/#/Debug/getStateV2 landed there for semi-accidental historical reasons, but it can't really be removed/hidden in a lot of cases, because it's used well outside of "debug" purposes, which means `debug` doesn't function well as a namespace one might, say, turn off or have lower compatibility threshold/guidelines on, so practically, `debug` interfaces tend to end up just as permanent and need just as much design as any others, not just slipped in because, whatever, `debug`, it's just for us PeerDAS testers

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: it might be interesting to have a truly-"debug" namespace, but right now it doesn't exist

excerpts.author: terencechain
excerpts.content:
My understanding is that there’s no “known bug” at the moment. The issue arose because some nodes were running outdated commits. Prysm has since upgraded to a more feature-complete commit. Could each client share an update on their status?

The main issue appears to be nodes advertising column subnets as available but being unable to serve them, which prevents other nodes from syncing to the head of the chain

One good topic for discussion (I won’t make this one since FOCIL is happening at the same time) is whether we plan to recover devnet6 or just start devnet7 at this point
